- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast rises >5% from prior day, cap next-day forecast at +3% of prior peak.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 65), model often overshoots; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic in early periods; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.5, 1.0, 0.0), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
